title: Ferrari's First EV Sells for Record $40 Million
paragraphs: Ferrari's first fully electric car has sold for $40 million, shattering the record for the most expensive new car ever sold at auction.
The Ferrari Luce "Chassis 0" was expected to sell for about $1.1 million, but bidding pushed the price to more than 35 times that amount.
"The bids kept climbing. Then, history was made," Ferrari USA wrote on Instagram after the auction, which was held in Monterey, California, on August 15.
All proceeds from the sale will go to the Ferrari Foundation to support educational projects, Ferrari said.

The Luce — which means "light" in Italian — is Ferrari's first fully electric car, and its first five-seater. The Chassis 0, the first production model of the car, features a white, pearl-like paint finish that changes color in the light, and a custom leather interior.
The car was designed by Jony Ive and Marc Newson, who both previously worked at Apple, where Ive helped design many of the company's most iconic products, including the iPhone and Apple Watch.

But the Luce received plenty of criticism when it was unveiled in May, with some saying it moved too far away from Ferrari's traditional designs with its electric power system and five-seat configuration. Ferrari's shares fell more than 8% following the launch.
Among those critics was former Ferrari chairman Luca di Montezemolo, who led the company for 23 years before stepping down in 2014.
"We're risking the destruction of a legend, and I'm truly sorry about that," he told the media.

With its bubble-like shape and softer design, the Luce looks very different from Ferrari's very angular supercars. Ferrari said earlier this year that it was "a different sort of Ferrari for a different sort of Ferrari client."
And the company appears to have found this new type of buyer, meeting its 2026 sales target within two months of launch, according to the Financial Times.
The car normally costs around $640,000, with delivery to customers expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.
